SOURCE-BASED ART DIRECTION · SEPTEMBER 2026

Build a city you can recognize.

Building and infrastructure catalogue for Sim City 2020. Every production brief is matched to a real tool in the supplied v0.4.0 code, its current rendering path, and ten proposed visual development stages.

37Surface objects5Network systems420Proposed art stages10 sUFO visit

Visual direction from your references

Carry forward the approved waterfront tower’s wall depth, staggered window bays and planted future-tower silhouette. Use these new images to give low-rise housing, shops, services and street infrastructure equally specific identities. Keep the player’s live map sharp; the strong tilt-shift blur in the references is optional presentation treatment, not the normal building mode.

What this release does. This is an artwork production catalogue, not a claim that 420 detailed models have been completed. The accompanying v0.4.1 patch adds the cosmetic UFO visit. The revised browser study removes its mirror-reflection pass. The full v0.4.0 game already uses colored water surfaces and has no equivalent mirrored reflection pass.

What the code review found

  • The tool registry contains exactly 48 entries: 37 surface objects, five independent networks, and six editing/inspection tools. Costs below are read directly from engine.mjs → TOOLS.
  • Building identity is spread across render.mjs, architecture.mjs and features.mjs. Schools, hospitals, police stations, fire stations, power plants and pumps use generic massing; bus and subway entries lack dedicated surface structures. They should be early artwork priorities.
  • The game has phases 1–10. Empty land is state 0, outside those ten built phases. Zoned buildings start at foundation phase 1. The earlier browser study used ten presentation scenes including empty land; those scene numbers are not a new save-game phase schema.
  • Many non-zone upgrades resize geometry or add repeated modules. Ten simulation levels do not currently mean ten distinct architectural designs. The phase-by-phase briefs below propose the missing visible differences.
  • The Three.js renderer converts common layer data; it is not yet a full architectural asset pipeline. Imported GLB and I3S remain tied to the deck.gl route. Replacing a placeholder requires an explicit model adapter and picking/overlay integration.
  • The default region is 16.384 × 12.288 km. Most facilities nevertheless occupy one 64 m parcel. Airports, major malls, dams and ports need multi-parcel reservations and valid infrastructure connections before full-scale models can be placed honestly.

Production standard for every asset

  1. Real geometry where silhouettes and shadows depend on it. Model window recesses, balcony edges, entrance canopies, parapets, roof machinery and major structural members. Use reusable facade modules and texture atlases for small repeated details.
  2. Complete the lot. Include an entrance, accessible route, service access, curbs, drains, planting and context-appropriate parking. Keep pavement connected to the road and people out of vehicle lanes.
  3. Keep simulation and artwork connected. Stable tool ID, phase, parcel ID, footprint, entrance sockets, utility sockets, foundation elevation and clearance envelope must accompany each model. Surface model origin is plot center at finished grade; keep one explicit conversion from glTF Y-up meters to the game’s Z-up coordinates.
  4. Material and light states. Separate base color, normal, roughness/metalness and emissive masks. Windows need depth and varied interior lighting. Wetness should change roughness; snow accumulates on exposed upper surfaces; seasons affect foliage. Keep shadow casting enabled on opaque structure and disabled where translucent glass produces implausible blocks.
  5. No upside-down duplicate below the scene. Do not add a planar scene-reflection render target. Water can use color, moving normals and bounded highlights. This also avoids a second full-scene render pass.
  6. Budget by visibility. Proposed starting budgets: houses 8–20k close-view triangles; civic/commercial lots 15–50k; landmarks 40–120k. These are targets to benchmark, not measured limits. Author at least three LODs, instance shared props, cap texture sizes, and test representative integrated graphics and software WebGL separately.
  7. Ten stages, consistent footprint. Keep entrances and service sockets stable across upgrades. Use construction scaffolding or staged replacement rather than uniformly stretching the entire building. Reserve expansion land before growing beyond a parcel; stages must not overlap neighbors.
  8. Acceptance views. Inspect front, side, rear, roof, street level, above and below ground where applicable. Review day, dusk, night, rain, snow, autumn and analytics coloring. Test placement previews, continuous painting, shadows, transparency, LOD swaps and return from camera cutscenes.

Six tools that are not buildings

IDToolCostArtwork scope
inspectInspect$0Selection feedback, not a permanent building mesh
reclaimReclaim land$1,500Temporary cursor/brush and terrain or demolition feedback; do not count as a building asset
raiseRaise terrain$350Temporary cursor/brush and terrain or demolition feedback; do not count as a building asset
lowerLower terrain$350Temporary cursor/brush and terrain or demolition feedback; do not count as a building asset
flattenLevel terrain$450Temporary cursor/brush and terrain or demolition feedback; do not count as a building asset
bulldozeBulldoze$40Temporary cursor/brush and terrain or demolition feedback; do not count as a building asset

The visitor: a harmless, rare comic event

SC20-UFO-VISITOR. Original saucer geometry inspired by reference C: a shallow metallic hull, raised blue-gray cockpit, articulated rim, 24 colored running lights, radial ribs and an underside emitter. The translucent green beam briefly lifts a tiny resident, then puts them back. No population, cash, condition, ownership or building is changed.

Active timeSequenceCamera
0–1.5 sSaucer approaches from offsite; rim lights rotate.Ease from the saved player view to the event.
1.5–3.3 sHover, scan, then open the green beam.Hold a clear three-quarter view.
3.3–6 sLift a puzzled resident in the beam.Keep both the saucer and ground visible.
6–7.5 sReturn the resident; caption: “Resident returned. Review: one star.”Remain steady.
7.5–8.5 sBeam shuts off; saucer accelerates away.Hold the neighborhood.
8.5–10 sClear all transient geometry.Ease back to the exact saved location, zoom, bearing, pitch and altitude.

Schedule one new random wait of 18–45 minutes after a visit starts. Count only eligible active play; hidden tabs, paused time, modal dialogs, held construction strokes, unfinished bridge placement and rocket tracking defer it. The simulation pauses during the visit and resumes in its previous state. An underground or orbital camera returns to its previous mode. Escape, Skip visit or touching the map restores the view early. Reduced-motion users get camera cuts. Enable/disable and preview are under City menu → City surprises. The remaining wait and enabled setting travel with JSON/SQLite saves; an active cutscene itself is never saved.

Implementation map

Source fileRole and player benefit
dist/engine.mjsAuthoritative tool registry, build validation, city simulation and save format. Keeps artwork tied to real player actions.
dist/development.mjsTen-phase names, growth gates and buildingForm dimensions. Defines which geometry changes should match an upgrade.
dist/render.mjsBase buildings, foundations, streets, trees, utilities and lighting. Main source of generic service-building silhouettes.
dist/architecture.mjsDestination-specific details, RCI trim, storefronts, parking stripes and lot trees. Starting point for modular facade kits.
dist/features.mjsSpecial facilities, bridges, arcologies, parking structures, moving traffic, trains, weather and rocket launches.
dist/three-renderer.mjsConverts common layer data into Three.js geometry and synchronizes camera/picking with the map. Does not load arbitrary ScenegraphLayer GLBs.
dist/graphics.mjsDeck renderer lifecycle and compatibility settings. Retains the alternative analytics renderer.
dist/geo.mjsWorld coordinates, terrain height, picking and camera presets. Models must share these transforms to avoid placement offset.
dist/terrain.mjsSix terrain presets and default 256 × 192 grid at 64 m per parcel (16.384 × 12.288 km).
dist/terrain-render.mjsTerrain meshes, colored water polygons and surrounding terrain. No mirrored building reflection pass exists here.
dist/construction.mjsContinuous held-pointer strokes, interpolation and construction transactions. Decorative meshes must not steal painting hits.
dist/launch.mjsRocket animation timeline. UFO visits defer while rocket tracking is active.
dist/analytics.mjsMetric definitions, colors, snapshots and animated analytic routes. Asset IDs must remain connected to parcel data.
dist/analytics-ui.mjsLayer controls and history inspection. Detailed facades must remain legible when an analytic overlay is active.
dist/climate.mjsSeason, weather, sun and launch conditions. Supplies visual state rather than physically exact weather.
dist/environment.mjsSimplified heat, carbon and runoff model. Wetland and tree artwork must not promise unimplemented physics.
dist/utilities.mjsConnectivity and capacity for water, power, metro, drainage and elevated rail.
dist/economy.mjsSector taxes, toll estimates, infrastructure wear and maintenance. Visible wear should stay subtle.
dist/opening.mjsStart screen, region selection and terrain import. No surprise events in map selection.
dist/workbench.mjsTools for weather, graphics, networks, bridges, imported models and launch control.
dist/upgrade-ui.mjsSQLite checkpoint UI, finance controls, audio settings and renderer switch.
dist/audio.mjsMusic progression and sound controls. This artwork/UFO patch does not replace the soundtrack.
dist/hud.mjsCollapsible controls and panels. Labels and event HUD should leave the model visible.
dist/icons.mjsBuild-tool icon definitions. New artwork retains the same tool identities.
dist/grid.mjsParcel indexing, dimensions and neighborhood queries.
dist/app.mjsConnects simulation, controls, renderer, save flow and UFO event controller.
dist/ufo.mjsNew: pure 10-second timeline, rare clock, target selection and camera interpolation.
dist/ufo-layers.mjsNew: original saucer, cockpit, lights, beam and visitor geometry shared by both renderers.
dist/ufo-ui.mjsNew: event scheduling, defer rules, saved camera restoration, skip and preview controls.
dist/terrain-import.mjsCSV and GeoJSON interpretation for editable terrain. Source imagery is visual reference, not imported height data.
server/server.pySQLite checkpoint service. Stored cities also retain the optional surprise-event waiting time.

Production order

First: a complete residential starter lot, strip mall, school, hospital, firehouse, bus shelter, metro entrance, parking court and park. These replace the most obvious missing identities and establish reusable street props. Second: industrial/utility plants, other civic services, destination buildings and garages. Third: large-scale airports, ports, dams, sculptural landmarks and mature future towers after their footprint and connection rules are implemented.
